arxiv-1903-12162.title: Self-organized synchronization of mechanically coupled resonators based on optomechanics gain-loss balance
arxiv-1903-12162.creator: P. Djorwé, Y. Pennec, B. Djafari-Rouhani
arxiv-1903-12162.description: Abstract We investigate self-organized synchronization in a blue-detuned optomechanical cavity that is mechanically coupled to an undriven mechanical resonator. By controlling the strength of the driving field, we engineer a mechanical gain that balances the losses of the undriven resonator. This gain-loss balance corresponds to the threshold where both coupled mechanical resonators enter simultaneously into self-sustained limit cycle oscillations regime.

arxiv-2010-11000.title: Techno-economic criteria to evaluate power flow allocation schemes
arxiv-2010-11000.creator: Fabian Hofmann, Alexander Zerrahn, Carlos Gaete-Morales
arxiv-2010-11000.description: Abstract We develop novel quantitative techno-economic evaluation criteria for power flow allocation schemes. Such schemes assign which nodes are responsible for which proportion of power flows on a line in a meshed electricity transmission network. As this allocation is, as such, indeterminate, the literature has proposed a number of dedicated schemes.

arxiv-2011-10644.title: Interacting hard-sphere fluids in an external field
arxiv-2011-10644.creator: Benaoumeur Bakhti, Gerhard Müller
arxiv-2011-10644.description: Abstract We present a new method for studying equilibrium properties of interacting fluids in an arbitrary external field. The fluid is composed of monodisperse spherical particles with hard-core repulsion and additional interactions of arbitrary shape and limited range. Our method of analysis is exact in one dimension and provides demonstrably good approximations in higher dimensions.

arxiv-2107-08199.title: Dynamic Transformer for Efficient Machine Translation on Embedded Devices
arxiv-2107-08199.creator: Hishan Parry, Lei Xun, Amin Sabet, Jia Bi, Jonathon Hare, Geoff V. Merrett
arxiv-2107-08199.description: Abstract The Transformer architecture is widely used for machine translation tasks. However, its resource-intensive nature makes it challenging to implement on constrained embedded devices, particularly where available hardware resources can vary at run-time. We propose a dynamic machine translation model that scales the Transformer architecture based on the available resources at any particular time.

arxiv-2109-04315.title: Yet another proof of the strong law of large numbers
arxiv-2109-04315.creator: Nicolas Curien
arxiv-2109-04315.description: Abstract We give a short proof of the strong law of large numbers based on duality for random walk. Let X_{1},X_{2},\dots be i.i.d. random variables with finite expectation and let S_{n}=X_{1}+\dots+X_{n} for n\geqslant 0 be the corresponding random walk. Kolmogorov’s strong law of large numbers says that n^{-1}S_{n}\to\mathbb{E}[X] almost surely as n\to\infty .

arxiv-2203-08479.title: Data Efficient 3D Learner via Knowledge Transferred from 2D Model
arxiv-2203-08479.creator: Ping-Chung Yu, Cheng Sun, Min Sun
arxiv-2203-08479.description: Abstract Collecting and labeling the registered 3D point cloud is costly. As a result, 3D resources for training are typically limited in quantity compared to the 2D images counterpart. In this work, we deal with the data scarcity challenge of 3D tasks by transferring knowledge from strong 2D models via RGB-D images.

arxiv-2301-00003.description: Abstract . This document presents endeavors to represent emotion in a computational cognitive architecture. The first part introduces research organizing with two axes of emotional affect: pleasantness and arousal. Following this basic of emotional components, the document discusses an aspect of emergent properties of emotion, showing interaction studies with human users.

arxiv-2303-17517.title: Hindi as a second language: Improving visually grounded speech with semantically similar samples
arxiv-2303-17517.creator: Hyeonggon Ryu*, Arda Senocak*, In So Kweon, Joon Son Chung
arxiv-2303-17517.description: Abstract The objective of this work is to explore the learning of visually grounded speech models (VGS) from multilingual perspective. Bilingual VGS models are generally trained with an equal number of spoken captions from both languages. However, in reality, there can be an imbalance among the languages for the available spoken captions.

arxiv-2406-15210.title: Assessing Effectiveness of Cyber Essentials Technical Controls
arxiv-2406-15210.creator: Priyanka Badva, Partha Das Chowdhury, Kopo M. Ramokapane, Barnaby Craggs, Awais Rashid
arxiv-2406-15210.description: Abstract Cyber Essentials (CE) comprise a set of controls designed to protect organisations, irrespective of their size, against cyber attacks. The controls are firewalls, secure configuration, user access control, malware protection & security update management . In this work, we explore the extent to which CE remains robust against an ever-evolving threat landscape.

arxiv-2409-04109.title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
arxiv-2409-04109.creator: Chenglei Si, Diyi Yang, Tatsunori Hashimoto
arxiv-2409-04109.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Chenglei Si, Diyi Yang, Tatsunori Hashimoto. Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have sparked optimism about their potential to accelerate scientific discovery, with a growing number of works proposing research agents that autonomously generate and validate new ideas. Despite this, no evaluations have shown that LLM systems can take the very first step of producing novel, expert-level ideas, let alone perform the entire research process.

arxiv-2410-17495.title: A Principled Basis for Nonequilibrium Network Flows
arxiv-2410-17495.creator: Ying-Jen Yang, Ken A. Dill
arxiv-2410-17495.description: Abstract The great power of EQuilibrium (EQ) statistical physics comes from its principled foundations: its First Law (conservation), Second Law (variational tendency principle), and its Legendre Transforms from observables ( U , V , N ) (U,V,N) to their driving forces ( T , p , μ ) (T,p,\mu) .

arxiv-2411-13177.title: Almost invariant subspaces of shift operators and products of Toeplitz and Hankel operators
arxiv-2411-13177.creator: Caixing Gu, In Sung Hwang, Hyoung Joon Kim, Woo Young Lee, Jaehui Park
arxiv-2411-13177.description: Abstract In this paper we formulate the almost invariant subspaces theorems of backward shift operators in terms of the ranges or kernels of product of Toeplitz and Hankel operators. This approach simplifies and gives more explicit forms of these almost invariant subspaces which are derived from related nearly backward shift invariant subspaces with finite defect.

arxiv-2507-09677.description: Abstract General relativistic static spherically symmetric (SSS) asymptotically flat configurations with scalar fields typically contain naked singularities at the center. We consider minimally coupled scalar fields with power-law potentials leading to the Coulomb asymptotic of the field ϕ ⁡ ( r ) ≈ Q / r \phi(r)\approx Q/r for large values of the radial variable r r .

pmc-13635178.creator: Ke Li, Jitai Yang, Yu Zhai, Hui Li
